adopted.summary: Point every plugin text at the two-step flow: `preview_*` returns plan + previewId, action takes only that previewId.
adopted.rationale:
- Read-only preview runs without a dialog; only the action prompts
- previewId lets the server tie the action to a real preview: same tool, same token, single use, 15 minutes
- Action args come from the stored preview, so action pages carry only `previewId`
- Write-tool header generated from readOnlyHint, so future write pages inherit the rule
- References rendered by the repo's own renderReference, so 22 untouched pages stay byte-identical

tour.title: Skill rules: act only on a previewId
tour.what:
- Prompt workflow: `preview_add_prompts`, show preview, then `add_prompts` with its `previewId`
- Article workflow: `preview_generate_article` for the credit cost, then `generate_article` with its `previewId`
- Rules: replaces 'call again with confirm=true' with 'act only on a previewId from the preview tool'
- Adds recovery: previewId single-use, 15 minutes; re-preview when expired
tour.why:
- SKILL.md is the model's operating rules: the real behaviour change in this repo
- Backend actions no longer accept `confirm` or content args, only `previewId`
tour.attention: Only expiry has a rule; redeem blocks, partial adds and cost drift leave the model unguided

evaluated.question: The 0.2.0 bump lands in plugin/plugin.json and plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json only. Do any other files carry a plugin version that should move with it (the marketplace manifests, the OpenAI/Codex package config read by scripts/package-openai.sh, package.json)? And does the session or the repo show what the manifest version actually drives for installed clients (update detection, cache key), or is that unknown?
evaluated.answer:
OTHER VERSION-BEARING FILES (inference from reading the repo, not from the session):
- .claude-plugin/marketplace.json: no `version` field. Its plugin entry is name, source "./plugin" and description only.
- .agents/plugins/marketplace.json (Codex): no `version` field. It has name, source {local, ./plugin}, policy and category.
- OpenAI/Codex package: there is no separate config. scripts/package-openai.sh zips plugin/ and leaves out mcp.json, .mcp.json and .claude-plugin/*. So plugin/plugin.json, now 0.2.0, IS the version the ZIP carries. Nothing else needs to move for it.
- package.json: "version": "0.1.0", unchanged. It is the private npm package for the scripts (`"private": true`), not a plugin manifest. Nothing in the repo reads it as the plugin version.
- scripts/generate-references.ts:18: `new Client({ name: "seerly-mcp-references", version: "0.1.0" })` is the MCP client name the script sends, not the plugin version.
- A grep for "version" across the repo (excluding .intent) finds only those four places. Both plugin manifests are at 0.2.0.

WHAT THE VERSION DRIVES, per the session (all from a web-fetch subagent's report on Anthropic's docs, read 2026-11-13, entry 6155; quoting the subagent, not the pages directly):
- Pre-submission check: "`description`, `author`, `version` missing: warning. Raise `version` with each release."
- Checklist item: "`version` raised each release".
- Directory updates: "merge to the tracked branch. The directory scans it. Raise `version` in `plugin.json`."
- Directory publishing default: "An Anthropic reviewer publishes each version." Other settings: "The reviewer publishes only the first version" or "You publish the first version."
- The session carried this into its submission pack (plans/2026-11-13-claude-directory-submission.md:114): "Updates: bump `version` in `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and merge to `main`." That is why both manifests moved.

UNKNOWN:
- Whether Claude Code or Codex use the manifest version for update detection or as a cache key on clients that installed from the self-hosted marketplace. The session never researched or tested it.
- The plugin is not yet listed in the directory, so the directory's per-version review does not apply to anyone today.

evaluated.question: SKILL.md now gives the model one recovery rule: 'if it has expired, preview again'. From the backend work in the session, what does add_prompts / generate_article return when the previewId is already used, was made under a different token, is unknown, or when the stored plan no longer holds at redeem time (credits spent or prompt limit reached since the preview)? Does the action re-check quota/credits at redeem, and is there any case where the model gets an error the skill gives it no rule for? If the transcript does not cover a case, say which.
evaluated.answer:
Mostly from the backend code on feat/mcp-write-previews (airo-backend-mcp-annotations). That is inference from code; I read it now. The session shows the tests and mutation runs, not a discussion of each case.

CASE BY CASE (src/core/mcp/tools/write-tools.ts):
- previewId unknown, already used, expired, made under a different access token, or made for the other write: all identical.
  - `take()` hashes tool + token + id into the Redis key and does GETDEL, so every one of these is a miss (write-preview-store.service.ts:46-54).
  - The action returns the error "That previewId is unknown, already used or expired. Call preview_<tool> again and show the user the new preview." (write-tools.ts:107-111).
  - The model cannot tell these cases apart. The error text itself gives the same instruction as the skill's "preview again".
- The previewed project is no longer on the connection: error "The previewed project is not on this connection. Preview the change again on the project you want." (write-tools.ts:112-113; project-for-args.ts:35-37). The message carries its own rule.

RE-CHECK AT REDEEM: YES. `runPlan(await spec.plan(...))` re-runs the whole plan with the stored args (write-tools.ts:114-128). The comment there: "The plan is worked out again at action time, so a limit reached since the preview still stops it."
- generate_article (generate-article.tool.ts:69-112):
  - re-reads plan limits and the latest strategy;
  - blocks with "An article costs X credits and Y are left. Credits can be bought in the Seerly app." or "Seerly did not report the article's credit cost...".
- add_prompts (add-prompts.tool.ts:68-108):
  - re-reads tracked prompts and the limit, and recomputes the selection;
  - blocks only when nothing is left to add: "The plan's prompt limit is reached." or "Every prompt is already tracked."
- A blocked redeem returns `{cannotProceed: <reason>, ...preview}` with isError true (write-tools.ts:130-135).

CASES THE SKILL HAS NO RULE FOR (inference):
1. Blocked at redeem.
   - The previewId is already consumed (GETDEL runs before the re-plan), so the model must preview again.
   - The skill's nearest rule, "A plan or subscription message means the user's plan does not include it: tell them, and do not retry", fits the prompt-limit case. It does not fit credits that ran out since the preview.
2. Partial add_prompts. If room shrank but is not zero, the action saves a SUBSET of what the user agreed to, with no block and no re-ask. The skill says nothing about reporting the difference.
3. generate_article cost drift. If the credit cost changed between preview and redeem and credits still cover it, the action runs at the new cost without re-asking.
4. execute() failure. If the backend write itself fails (`outcome.kind !== "ok"`, write-tools.ts:124-127), the model gets `errorResult(reason)` and the previewId is already spent. There is no skill rule.
5. The preview itself blocked. `preview_*` returns cannotProceed and no previewId (write-tools.ts:70). There is no explicit skill rule, though the reason text is shown.

WHAT THE SESSION ACTUALLY TESTED (write-tools.spec.ts test names; 10 pass):
- "preview_add_prompts hands out no previewId once the plan's prompt limit is reached"
- "add_prompts saves nothing when the prompt limit was reached after the preview"
- "preview_generate_article refuses when credits are short, and hands out no previewId"
- "a write without a previewId Seerly handed out changes nothing"
- "a previewId acts once, so a repeated call does not write twice"
- "a previewId opens only the write and the connection it was made for"

NOT tested, going by the names:
- credits running short between preview and redeem;
- the partial-add path;
- TTL expiry (the fake Redis's handling of EX is not shown);
- an execute() failure after the id is consumed;
- the out-of-scope project at redeem.

None of these cases was discussed with the user.

evaluated.question: Rollout window: once the backend deploys, a client still holding the 0.1.0 skill text sends confirm=true to an action that only takes previewId; until it deploys, the 0.2.0 text names preview_* tools prod lacks. Was a transition considered in the session (backend briefly accepting both, or merging plugin and backend together), and does the session show whether installed plugins pick up main automatically or only on a manual update? If not covered, say so.
evaluated.answer:
TRANSITION: not considered in the session.
- The backend dropped `confirm` outright. Assistant at 6781: "Source changes are in, with no `confirm` left outside the tests."
- No dual-accept window, and no plan to merge plugin and backend together, appears anywhere.
- The only ordering is sequential, written by the assistant into the submission pack (plans/2026-11-13-claude-directory-submission.md):
  - line 9: backend PR "merged, deployed and promoted";
  - line 10: the seerly-mcp PR "merged after the backend is on prod".
  - The user did not discuss it.
- Deploy mechanics from earlier in the session: merging the backend deploys to the green staging slot, and a separate promote takes it to prod. The window opens at promote and lasts until the plugin is merged AND clients refresh.

DO INSTALLED PLUGINS PICK UP MAIN AUTOMATICALLY? Not covered.
- The session's research (early on) says a self-hosted marketplace is published "by pushing it. There is no review step. Users run `claude plugin marketplace add <source>`, then `claude plugin install name@marketplace`" (entries 71/73), and the Codex equivalent is `codex plugin marketplace add`. It never says whether installed copies refresh on their own or need a manual update.
- Directory listings, per the subagent at 6155: "An Anthropic reviewer publishes each version" by default. But the plugin is not yet submitted, so today every install is from the self-hosted marketplace (the user installed it from the public repo in an earlier context).
- The OpenAI/ChatGPT portal takes an uploaded ZIP, so that copy changes only on a manual re-upload. Not done.

WHAT THE WINDOW COSTS (inference from the backend code, not discussed in the session):
- Tool schemas and descriptions come live from seerly.app, not from the plugin. After the backend deploys:
  - a 0.1.0 client still sees `preview_*` in tools/list;
  - it sees an action whose only argument is a required `previewId`;
  - it sees a description saying "Runs only with a previewId from preview_<tool>".
- A stale `confirm=true` call carrying the old arguments has no previewId, so it fails input validation and writes nothing. That fails closed: worse UX, no data risk.
- Before the backend deploys, a 0.2.0 skill naming `preview_*` gets tool-not-found. The live `add_prompts` / `generate_article` still preview when called without `confirm`, so that also fails safe.
- Both are reasoned from code. Neither was run.
